summary: Construct a coefficient-rational Hodge correspondence between equal-signature quaternionic Shimura varieties. The plan combines an explicit hermitian exterior-square comparison, harmonic theta classes with simultaneous sign nonvanishing, the unitary cohomological eigenspace calculation, and rational determinant descent. The all-prime Galois assertion retains Kottwitz’s conjecture as an explicit hypothesis. General Shimura, realization and theta machinery is imported from its owners; missing supplier interfaces are recorded precisely.

nodes.title: Jacquet–Langlands Hodge data
nodes.statement: Fix a totally real field F of degree n, quaternion algebras B₁,B₂ with the same set Σ of split real places, d=|Σ|<n, and a cuspidal GL₂(A_F) representation π with trivial central character, even weights k_v≥2, and transfers π_i to B_i×. Put L=Q(π), containing Q(k). Use the unitary normalization r=0 and the coefficient representation τ_k=⊗_v Nrd_v^{(2−k_v)/2} Sym^{k_v−2}(τ_v), with its dual local system. F_Σ is the fixed field of automorphisms preserving Σ. An L-Hodge structure means a rational Hodge structure with L-action; equivalently use every embedding of L, rather than assuming conjugation preserves one arbitrary L-embedding. When d=0 use the finite compact Shimura set and its trivial-cocharacter constant model over Q; do not require Deligne’s exclusion of compact Q-adjoint factors for this degenerate case.

nodes.title: The division-algebra reduction

nodes.title: Archimedean sign lines
nodes.statement: For V_i of multiplicity-realization, its complexification decomposes into 2^d one-dimensional tensor sign lines indexed by signs at v∈Σ. At a split v the two cochain contributions have bidegrees (1,0) and (0,1); their actual coefficient-normalized Hodge types are (k_v/2,1−k_v/2) and the reversed pair. Outside Σ the degree-zero coefficient line contributes (0,0). Equal total Hodge types can have multiplicity, so retain the full tensor-sign indexing. The duality pairs opposite signs.

nodes.statement: Let H be the Q(k)-rational Hecke space of hecke-eigenspace and W_Q the invariant component space of component-galois-invariants. Fix L-rational finite representation parameters as in restriction-correspondence. The determinant of Res_c(x) is a polynomial in coordinates of x∈H and c∈W_Q, with coefficients in L. Complex-invertibility and c_η∈W_Q⊗C give a complex point where it is nonzero. Since Q(k) and Q are infinite, choose x∈H and c∈W_Q at which it remains nonzero, treating the two parameter blocks successively. The resulting tensor ξ₀ has coefficients L, is Hodge by purity of every conjugate summand, and is invertible.
hypotheses: Use the fields and dimensions explicitly fixed in the statement; where E/F occurs it is quadratic of characteristic zero, with the local quadratic-étale variant only where stated.

Global automorphic and cohomological assertions use Jacquet–Langlands Hodge data, its fixed unitary coefficient normalization, sufficiently small compatible finite levels, and the nonzero cuspidal lifts explicitly required in the statement.
proofSteps: Write the determinant of the bilinear family in finite-dimensional bases; nonzero at a complex point means it is not the zero polynomial.

For the theta block, expand the finitely many L-valued coefficients over Q(k) and choose a nonzero coordinate polynomial. Apply homogeneous polynomial nonvanishing over Q(k), leaving a nonzero polynomial in c. Then expand its coefficients over Q and apply the same argument over Q to the component block. This is not averaging.
Use purity of every coefficient conjugate to make the rational theta vector a Hodge vector, then apply the Hodge-compatible restriction map.
acceptance: Averaging an arbitrary invertible operator need not remain invertible, so cannot replace the determinant argument.
